note: One people, tradition or figure from history for every African country. Named as themselves: the Dogon are the Dogon, not 'a Malian'.

AGO.name: Ovimbundu
AGO.note: The largest of Angola's peoples, farmers and traders of the high plateau.

BDI.name: Royal drummer of Burundi
BDI.note: Drums carried on the head, played by whole teams at once.

BEN.name: Agojie
BEN.note: The women soldiers of the kingdom of Dahomey.

BFA.name: Mossi
BFA.note: Horse riders who built kingdoms on the bend of the Volta.

BWA.name: San
BWA.note: Trackers of the Kalahari, who can read a day-old footprint.

CAF.name: Aka
CAF.note: Forest people whose singing weaves many voices at once.

CIV.name: Senufo
CIV.note: Carvers and mask dancers of the northern savanna.

CMR.name: Bamileke
CMR.note: People of the grassfields, known for beaded masks and elephant dancers.

COD.name: Mbuti
COD.note: Hunters of the Ituri forest, at home under the tallest trees.

COG.name: Kongo
COG.note: People of an old kingdom on both banks of the great river.

COM.name: Grand Mariage dancer
COM.note: A wedding that lasts days and makes a man an elder.

CPV.name: Morna singer
CPV.note: Songs of the sea and of missing home, sung with a guitar.

DJI.name: Afar
DJI.note: Herders of one of the hottest places on Earth.

DZA.name: Kabyle
DZA.note: Amazigh people of the mountains, with a language of their own.

ERI.name: Rashaida
ERI.note: Camel herders of the Red Sea coast, in silver and red veils.

ETH.name: Hamar
ETH.note: Cattle keepers of the Omo valley, in ochre and beads.

GAB.name: Fang
GAB.note: Carvers of guardian figures that watch over the ancestors.

GHA.name: Asante
GHA.note: The kingdom of the Golden Stool, and of kente cloth.

GIN.name: Fula
GIN.note: Herders who move across a dozen countries with their cattle.

GMB.name: Griot
GMB.note: Keepers of a family's history, who sing it rather than write it.

GNB.name: Bijagó
GNB.note: Islanders of eighty islands, with dances that become animals.

GNQ.name: Bubi
GNQ.note: The first people of the island of Bioko.

LBR.name: Kpelle
LBR.note: Farmers of the forest, with masks that teach as they dance.

LBY.name: Tuareg
LBY.note: The blue-veiled people of the Sahara, who cross it by camel.

LSO.name: Basotho horseman
LSO.note: A pony, a blanket and a mountain path — how you travel here.

MAR.name: Amazigh
MAR.note: The people of the Atlas, whose name means 'free people'.

MDG.name: Vezo
MDG.note: Fishing people of the west coast, who sail outrigger canoes.

MLI.name: Dogon
MLI.note: Cliff dwellers of Bandiagara, with masks as tall as a house.

MOZ.name: Makonde carver
MOZ.note: Whole families carved from one piece of blackwood.

MRT.name: Imraguen
MRT.note: Fishers who wade into the surf, and fish with the help of dolphins.

MWI.name: Gule Wamkulu dancer
MWI.note: The great dance of the Chewa, danced by masked spirits.

NAM.name: Himba
NAM.note: Cattle herders of the far north, in red ochre and braids.

NER.name: Wodaabe
NER.note: Herders whose young men dance a beauty contest at Gerewol.

NGA.name: Yoruba
NGA.note: People of Ile-Ife, of talking drums and bronze heads.

RWA.name: Intore dancer
RWA.note: The dance of heroes, with grass headdresses that swing like manes.

SAH.name: Sahrawi
SAH.note: Desert people of the western Sahara, in indigo and tents.

SDN.name: Nubian
SDN.note: People of the Nile with pyramids older than some in Egypt.

SDS.name: Dinka
SDS.note: Cattle keepers who name themselves after their favourite ox.

SEN.name: Wolof
SEN.note: People of the sabar drum, played with a hand and a stick.

SLE.name: Mende
SLE.note: The only place in Africa where women wear the great masks.

SOL.name: Somali camel herder
SOL.note: More camels here than almost anywhere on Earth.

SOM.name: Somali camel herder
SOM.note: More camels here than almost anywhere on Earth.

STP.name: Tchiloli player
STP.note: A street play five hundred years old, performed in masks.

SWZ.name: Swazi reed dancer
SWZ.note: Thousands dance to the royal village carrying cut reeds.

TCD.name: Toubou
TCD.note: People of the Tibesti mountains, in the middle of the desert.

TGO.name: Batammariba
TGO.note: Builders of clay tower-houses that look like little castles.

TUN.name: Amazigh
TUN.note: At Matmata they live in houses dug down into the ground.

UGA.name: Baganda
UGA.note: People of the kingdom of Buganda, on the shore of the great lake.

ZAF.name: Zulu
ZAF.note: People of the shield and the beaded message, in KwaZulu.

ZMB.name: Lozi of the Kuomboka
ZMB.note: When the flood comes, the king moves house by barge.

ZWE.name: Shona stone carver
ZWE.note: Builders of Great Zimbabwe, and carvers of its birds.
